1  SESSIONS JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS  TRIBUNAL, BELAGAVI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR  COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION  AND ETC.,
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB  MFA No. 102960 of 2018  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, G BASAVARAJA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant has preferred this appeal against the judgment and award passed by the learned IX Addl. District and Sessions Judge and AMACT, Belagavi (for short 'Tribunal') in M.V.C. No. 77/2016 dated 04.04.2018 seeking for enhancement of compensation.
Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

2. The brief relevant facts leading to this appeal is that the petitioner/claimant has filed claim petition u/S 166 of M.V. Act seeking compensation for injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

It is stated that on 01.05.2015 at about 11.00 a.m. near Vattulli village limits when the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider on motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 22-EQ-0689, its rider rode the same in high speed, rash and negligent manner and lost control over it in a curve and caused the accident, thereby he has sustained injuries; he was treated as inpatient and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment.
He is still under follow up treatment.
Due to the accident he has suffered permanent physical injuries.
The accident had NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by its rider.
Injured was aged 65 years and earning Rs.15,000/- per month as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondents no.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer respectively, are liable to pay compensation.
3. Respondent no. 1 was placed exparte.
Respondent no.2- insurer appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections contending that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
The petitioner having sustained injuries otherwise than by involvement of said motorcycle, implicated the same in collusion with respondent no.1.
The rider of the motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed appropriate issues.
To prove the case of the claimant, two witnesses were examined as PWs.1 and 2 and 18 documents were marked as Exs.P.1 to P.18.
On closure of petitioner's side evidence, respondents have not adduced any evidence but marked Ex.R.1 and R.2.

Having heard arguments of both NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB sides, the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.1,93,135/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Being aggrieved by this judgment and Arjun Ramanna Patil vs Shankar Yellari Patil on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53848368/
2 award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is contrary to law; it erred in not considering that the appellant was earning Rs.15,000/-
per month; Ex.P.2-complaint reveals that appellant was agriculturist; income of the appellant is taken on the lower side; the Tribunal erred in not considering that the appellant had suffered fracture of clavicle right, fracture of zydontic bone right with head injury.

The appellant has got 30%
permanent physical disability to right lower limb.
The Tribunal erred in considering the functional disability of body as 20% and loss of earning capacity as 7%.

It also erred in not considering the amount spent by the petitioner, i.e., a sum of Rs.1,19,005/- towards medical expenses, which is evident from Ex.P.8, hospital bill which includes Shri Siddhi Vinayak Hospital bill of Rs.33,150/-
has not been considered.
The Tribunal has erred in NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB not granting attendant charges, etc. as per the decision of the Apex Court and not awarded compensation towards loss of amenities.
The Tribunal has awarded very meager compensation and sought for enhancement of compensation.

6. As against this, learned counsel for respondent would submit that the Tribunal has awarded compensation in accordance with law and facts which needs no interference and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
7. Having heard the arguments of both sides and on perusal of appeal papers, the following points would arise for our consideration.
1) Whether the appellant/claimant is entitled for compensation as sought for?
2) What order of award?

8. Our answers to the above points are as under:
 Point No. 1 : Partly in the affirmative  Point No. 2 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 9.
We have examined the materials placed before this Court.
There is no dispute as to the accident.
It is also not in dispute NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB as to the injuries caused to the petitioner.
Ex . P.6
-wound certificate of the petitioner reveals that he has sustained comminuted fracture of right clavicle, fracture of orbital wall and fracture of zygomatic.
Ex.P.11 is the discharge card of the petitioner reveals that he was admitted as inpatient on 01.05.2015 and discharged on 12.05.2015.
Ex.P.13 to P.15 are X-ray reports, Ex.P.16 is CT brain plain report, Ex.P.17 is the disability certificate and Ex.P.18 is the X-ray films.

sentences.text: PW-2 has stated that petitioner has got permanent physical disability to the extent of 30% in respect of right upper limb.
Admittedly, PW2 is not a treated Doctor.
It is not in dispute that age of the petitioner was 65 years at the time of accident.

Considering his age, occupation and the medical evidence, the Tribunal has assessed notional disability at the rate of 7% to the whole body which is quite reasonable and does not call for interference.

11. With regard to the notional income of the claimant is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed notional income of the claimant at the rate of Rs.6,000/- per month instead of Rs.8,000/- as prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB Authority.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB Authority
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appellant-claimant is entitled for Rs.47,040/- (Rs. 8,000/- x 12 x 7 x 7%) towards loss of income as against Rs.35,280/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. The petitioner has claimed an amount of Rs.1,19,005/- towards medical expenses under Ex.P.8 which includes Shri Siddhi Vinayak Hospital bill of Rs.33,150/-.

The Tribunal has observed that this bill is dated after eight months from the date of accident as the petitioner got admitted in Shri Siddhi Vinayak Hospital on 21.01.2016 and discharged on 29.01.2016.
Ex.P.12-discharge summary issued by the said hospital reveals that petitioner was treated for hernia disease.

Hence, Rs.33,150/-
is deducted which is not pertaining to the accidental injuries and awarded Rs.85,855/- towards medical expenses.
The said finding of the Tribunal needs no interference.

13. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering;
Rs.12,000/- towards food, transportation and attendant charges including loss of income during stay in the hospital; a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded NC: 2024:KHC-D:9830-DB towards loss of amenities in life and a sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses.

14. Considering the age, occupation and treatment period as inpatient, pain and suffering, we deem it appropriate to modify the award as under:
1. Pain and suffering 50,000.00 2. Food, transportation and attendant 20,000.00 charges 3. Loss of earning during laid up period 24,000.00 (for 3 months)
4. Medical expenses (as awarded by the 85,855.00 Tribunal)
5.

Future medical expenses (as awarded 5,000.00 by the Tribunal)
6. Loss of amenities 30,000.00 7.
Loss of future income 47,040.00
Award of the Tribunal 1,93,135.00
Enhancement 68,760.00
Hence, point no.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
